cards.explanation: The answer is that John wants to know if Jesus is the One who was to come. John sends two of his disciples with one question, and it's a big one: "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" (Luke 7:19) No small talk, no warm-up. I wish my questions were that tidy, friends, because mine show up with a ten-minute introduction.

The answer is True. The passage says that at that very hour Jesus healed many people of their diseases, afflictions and evil spirits, and He gave sight to many who were blind (Luke 7:21). John's men show up with a question, and that's the hour this is happening. That's like asking if the bakery is open while you're smelling cookies from the sidewalk.

The answer is what they have seen and heard. Jesus says, "Go back and report to John what you have seen and heard…" (Luke 7:22) He doesn't give a plain yes or no. He sends them back with what's right in front of them. Those two just watched Jesus heal people, so they're carrying an eyewitness report.

The answer is the poor. Jesus ends His list with "…and the good news is preached to the poor." (Luke 7:22) It comes right after the blind, the lame, the lepers, the deaf and the dead. It's the last item, friends, and it's easy to rush past.

The answer is the one who does not fall away because of Him. Jesus says, "Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me." (Luke 7:23) That's the last thing He says to John's messengers. John asked a question, and Jesus answers with what they've seen and then this blessing.

The answer is False. Jesus says, "Look, those who wear elegant clothing and live in luxury are found in palaces." (Luke 7:25) Palaces, not the wilderness. His point is that the crowds didn't go out there to see a man in fine clothes.

The answer is yes, and more than a prophet. Jesus answers His own question: "A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet." (Luke 7:26) John is a prophet, and Jesus says he is more than that. It's a big answer to a simple question.

The answer is prepare. Jesus quotes, "Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way before You." (Luke 7:27) The messenger goes first and gets the way ready. That's the job Jesus says is written about John.

The answer is False. Jesus says no one born of women is greater than John. Then He adds, "…yet even the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he." (Luke 7:28) Read it slowly, friends, because it's a lot to take in.

The answer is that they had received John's baptism. That's the reason the passage gives: "For they had received the baptism of John." (Luke 7:29) The tax collectors are named on purpose. Even they acknowledged God's justice, and the text ties it to John's baptism.

The answer is that they reject it. The text says the Pharisees and experts in the law "rejected God’s purpose for themselves, because they had not been baptized by John." (Luke 7:30) That sits right next to the people who received John's baptism and acknowledged God's justice. It's the opposite response.

The answer is that the others did not dance or weep. The children call out, "We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a dirge, and you did not weep." (Luke 7:32) They played a happy tune and a sad one, and they didn't get the response they wanted either way. That's a tough crowd.

The answer is that they find fault with him. John came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and Jesus says people respond, "He has a demon!" (Luke 7:33) Faultfinding is what Jesus describes. John came one way and still got criticized.

The answer is False. Jesus says the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and people said, "Look at this glutton and drunkard, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!" (Luke 7:34) That isn't approval. It's the same crowd with a new complaint.
The answer is right. Jesus says, "But wisdom is vindicated by all her children." (Luke 7:35) Vindicated means proven right. It's His closing line after both John and the Son of Man got criticized.
